doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Attitudes toward women bands, then and with Diva
summary: Venues and musicians make condescending remarks about Diva, showing how ingrained gender assumptions are.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: She told me a very, very similar story about a jam session situation.

Well it’s funny it happens with Diva also. We’ll go to a venue and people, I mean people have actually said things to us as stupid as, “well even the professional bands don’t do this,” you know, meaning if we question their sound system or something. So you just look back at them with — what — and then of course the band plays and then usually the people become almost apologetic for their stupidity, you know, once they hear the band. Another known musician recently said, “God you guys sound so great, almost like a real band.” And you just look at them like — and then they try to back pedal — I didn’t mean that. Like okay. And so it’s always really interesting and it’s so funny. I mean it’s not funny it’s common how slow, the stuff that’s socially ingrained in people’s mind about what women do and what men do. It just takes so long to change it, if it ever will change, I don’t know.
Do you think people would — I’m not sure how to even ask this — how would it change the look or the perception of your band if there was like three men in it? © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
